description: Northridge has a mix of family homes, student-adjacent rentals, and established neighborhoods where HVAC performance matters through long hot summers. Bernardino Martin helps Northridge customers solve cooling issues, maintain airflow, and plan equipment upgrades that support dependable comfort without overspending on guesswork or short-term fixes.
climate: Hot valley conditions with extended summer use and dry winter air

localLife.nature: Much of Northridge's housing stock was rebuilt or retrofitted after the 1994 earthquake, which means a newer mix of code-compliant construction sits alongside older buildings that survived and were shored up rather than replaced.
localLife.community: A steady student-renter population cycling through apartments near CSUN, family households in the surrounding blocks, and a local economy that runs on the university's semester calendar as much as anything else.
localLife.howWeHelp: We know the difference between servicing a system in a building rebuilt to post-1994 code and one in an older structure that was retrofitted rather than replaced, and we work around the surge of move-ins and move-outs that comes with a campus calendar.

seasonalNotes.focus: Long, hot valley summers push both post-quake rebuilds and older retrofitted buildings hard — the difference in ductwork age between the two is often the real story behind a system that's struggling.
Move-in season near CSUN each fall means a wave of new tenants inheriting whatever system the last renter left behind — we get called in to find out what's actually wrong with it.
